title: Event trace
preamble:
# Event trace

The canonical form for recording, replaying, and simulating
DS sessions. The event trace is the single artefact through
which DS's determinism, testability, and debuggability
guarantees are realised.

The conformance surface is the **typed in-memory event
sequence** every conforming runtime delivers through its
stream callback. Every event has the same envelope shape
(seq + clock_ns + source + event_id + kind-discriminated
payload). On-disk capture format is integrator territory:
the integrator picks how the typed events get to bytes
(protobuf, JSON-lines, CBOR, bespoke, nothing-at-all). The
content the integrator records is fixed; the encoding is
their choice.

## What this is not

- Not a wire protocol for adapter ↔ engine traffic at runtime.
  Adapter ingest is integrator-driven; the event trace is
  what the engine *emits* for observable events after they
  enter or leave it.
- Not an on-disk encoding spec. The runtime delivers a
  typed event sequence to the integrator's callback;
  recording format (protobuf, JSON, custom, none) is the
  integrator's choice. A protobuf schema is provided as
  an interoperability reference (see [LFST.2]) but is
  not normative.
- Not a metrics / telemetry surface. See §Out of stream
  scope.
- Not a debugger protocol — debugger bridges layer on top
  of the existing stream callback.
- Not prescriptive about how recordings are stored, rotated,
  compressed, or archived — operational choices.
